findings.highlight: a lot of people are needed to restock inventory.
findings.evidenceJa: 棚卸しには何人もの人手が必要になる。
findings.governingReading: Copenhagen needs several workers for 棚卸し, taking or checking inventory; the task requires at least five people and becomes easier with more.
findings.explanation: Restock inventory changes an accounting and stock-checking job into replenishing shelves, repeating the wrong task already found in the prior employment passage.

findings.highlight: before we realized, two hours had passed and we’d finished restocking the inventory.
findings.evidenceJa: 気が付けば二時間後、棚卸しは予定通り終わっていた。
findings.governingReading: Two hours later, the stocktaking has been completed on schedule.
findings.explanation: The English repeats restocking at the completion point, confirming that the scene-wide job has been changed rather than suffering one stray word choice.

findings.highlight: The family is well balanced, as the boss likes sweet things while his daughter likes spicy things.
findings.evidenceJa: ここの一家は店長が甘党で娘さんが辛党という、バランスのいい嗜好をしていらっしゃる。
findings.governingReading: The household is comically balanced: the father has a sweet tooth and eats rum cake, while his daughter is a drinker and has hot sake; 辛党 carries its alcohol-preferring sense here.
findings.explanation: Likes spicy things selects the literal-looking but contextually wrong sense of 辛党 and breaks the explicit cake-versus-sake contrast.

findings.highlight: so you came here today even though you didn’t have to?
findings.evidenceJa: なに、じゃあ今日の棚卸し、また聞きだったのに来たんだ
findings.governingReading: Neko is incredulous that Shirou came to the stocktaking even though he heard of it secondhand rather than receiving the request directly.
findings.explanation: Didn’t have to replaces the information-channel distinction with general lack of obligation, deleting why Neko next treats both Furumi and Shirou as foolish.

findings.highlight: She seems to think I’m a firefly or something.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺をトンボか何かと勘違いしているっぽい。
findings.governingReading: Watching Neko circle a finger as she speaks, Shirou jokes that she seems to have mistaken him for a dragonfly, invoking the familiar image of a dragonfly visually following a circling finger.
findings.explanation: Firefly substitutes a different insect with no corresponding finger-following mechanism, so the observed gesture no longer motivates the comparison.
